title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages). Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, a free profinite group on two generators with three distinguished inertia conjugacy classes x, y, z (xyz=1). M_{0,3}^~ is the 'Teichmüller-type' extension: automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} that preserve the set of three inertia classes up to a common power. N_{0,3}^~ = M_{0,3}^~/Π̂_{0,3} is the corresponding group of outer automorphisms. Permuting the three classes gives N^~ → S_3 with kernel N^{~!}. The previous page (11) asserts N^~ ≅ S_3 × N^{~!}.

This page, step by step.

(13)-(14): An element of M^~ sends each inertia generator to a conjugate of its λ-th power, for a common λ ∈ Ẑ^*. Grothendieck calls this the 'multiplication' (multiplier). This gives a character χ: M^~ → Ẑ^*, the abstract analogue of the cyclotomic character.
- χ is surjective. This is already clear from Γ_Q, whose cyclotomic character is onto.
- χ kills Π̂_{0,3} (inner automorphisms have multiplier 1), so it factors through N^~ (15).
- χ also kills the S_3 of 'pure permutations', which have multiplier 1. Using (11) it is therefore regarded as a character of N^~/S_3 ≅ N^{~!}.

(16)-(17): The kernels M^{+~} and N^{+~} of χ give a morphism of extensions of Ẑ^*. The second row is the quotient of the first by Π̂_{0,3}.

(18): Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄_0/Q_0), with Q̄_0 the algebraic closure of Q in C, embeds canonically in N^{~!}. This is the outer Galois action on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}_{Q̄}). It lands in the inertia-preserving outer automorphisms with multiplier the cyclotomic character. It commutes with S_3, since the S_3 symmetries are defined over Q. Injectivity is Belyi's theorem.

The page then turns to complex conjugation τ (continued on the next page). The next page defines M_{0,3} as the inverse image of S_3 × Γ_Q and states the programme: compute N^{~!} explicitly, then find as many necessary conditions as possible for an element of N^{~!} to come from Γ_Q, ideally a (conjectural) characterization.

Purpose: to set up the ambient 'combinatorial' group in which Γ_Q sits, i.e. the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme, here in its genus 0, 3-point stage. The 'équation des lacets' is the source of the relations to be imposed.
errors: Possible gap inherited from (11) of the previous page and used in (15). A canonical section S_3 → N^~ only gives a semidirect product N^~ ≅ N^{~!} ⋊ S_3. A direct product, and hence N^~/S_3 as a quotient group isomorphic to N^{~!}, requires S_3 to be normal, i.e. central relative to N^{~!}. If N^~ is the full group of inertia-preserving outer automorphisms, this fails: commutation with the S_3 symmetries is exactly what the later literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps) encodes in the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations defining GT.
The statements about χ are unaffected, since χ restricted to N^{~!} is a homomorphism and S_3 has multiplier 1. Γ_Q does commute with S_3, so (18) is fine.
Minor: injectivity in (18) is a deep theorem (Belyi 1979, for P^1 minus 3 points), not a formal consequence; the page states it without comment.

ideas.what: Multiplier character χ: automorphisms of π̂_1(P^1−3 pts) preserving inertia classes up to a common power λ, giving a surjection to Ẑ^* and extensions with kernels M^{+~}, N^{+~}
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic-type character on Out^♯(F̂_2) / on GT (the λ-component of (λ,f) ∈ GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); Out^♯ studied by Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Circulated in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this precise formalism appears only in these notes as far as known

ideas.what: Canonical embedding Γ_Q ↪ N_{0,3}^{~!} (outer Galois action on the profinite π_1 of the thrice-punctured line)
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness of the outer Galois representation, Belyi's theorem

ideas.what: Programme: compute the combinatorial group N^{~!} and seek necessary (ultimately characterizing) conditions for its elements to come from Γ_Q
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme (GT ⊇ Γ_Q, the question whether GT = Γ_Q)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984); La Longue Marche (1981, circulated)

deep.surprise_reason: This is notation and set-up for the genus-0, 3-point Teichmüller tower: the multiplier character, the kernels and the Belyi embedding. All of it corresponds to well-known later material (Out^♯, GT, Belyi). It is historically nice as an early formulation of the 'characterize Γ_Q inside an explicit group' programme, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: (13): the middle group appears to be written \hat{\hat{\mathfrak S}}_{0,3} (double hat) with 'multiplication' written above the arrow labelled χ; the transcription is plausible.
(15): the bottom of the triangle reads 'N_{0,3}^{~}/S_3 ≃ N_{0,3}^{~!}' (the '!' superscript is clear in the image).

The final line is not 'Négligeant les autres [?] de conjugaison'. The words 'dans C' above the line belong to the annotation under \overline{Q}_0 ('clôture alg. de Q dans C'). The line likely reads something like '[Indiquons/Notons] l'automorphisme de conjugaison [complexe τ]', continuing on the next page.
